1.1: And these are the names of the sons of Israel who are coming into Egypt with Jacob; a man and his household have they come;
1.4: Dan, and Naphtali, Gad, and Asher.
1.5: And all the persons coming out of the thigh of Jacob are seventy persons; as to Joseph, he was in Egypt.
1.6: And Joseph dies, and all his brethren, and all that generation;
1.7: and the sons of Israel have been fruitful, and they teem, and multiply, and are very very mighty, and the land is filled with them.
1.8: And there rises a new king over Egypt, who has not known Joseph,
1.9: and he says to his people, `Indeed, the people of the sons of Israel is more numerous and mighty than we;
1.10: give help! let us act wisely concerning it, lest it multiply, and it has come to pass, when war happens, that it has been joined, even it, to those hating us, and has fought against us, and has gone out up of the land.'
1.11: And they set over it princes of tribute, so as to afflict it with their burdens, and it builds store-cities for Pharaoh, Pithom and Raamses;
1.12: and as they afflict it, so it multiplies, and so it breaks forth, and they are vexed because of the sons of Israel;
1.13: and the Egyptians cause the sons of Israel to serve with rigour,
1.14: and make their lives bitter in hard service, in clay, and in brick, and in every kind of service in the field; all their service in which they have served is with rigour.
1.15: And the king of Egypt speaks to the midwives, the Hebrewesses, (of whom the name of the one is Shiphrah, and the name of the second Puah),
1.16: and says, `When you cause the Hebrew women to bear, and have looked on the children; if it is a son--then you have put him to death; and if it is a daughter--then she has lived.'
1.17: And the midwives fear God, and have not done as the king of Egypt has spoken to them, and keep the lads alive;
1.18: and the king of Egypt calls for the midwives, and says to them, `Wherefore have you done this thing, and keep the lads alive?'
1.19: And the midwives say to Pharaoh, `Because the Hebrew women are not as the Egyptian women, for they are lively; before the midwife comes in to them--they have borne!'
1.20: And God does good to the midwives, and the people multiply, and are very mighty;
1.21: and it comes to pass, because the midwives have feared God, that He makes for them households;
1.22: and Pharaoh lays a charge on all his people, saying, `Every son who is born--into the River you do cast him, and every daughter you do keep alive.'

2.1: And there goes a man of the house of Levi, and he takes the daughter of Levi,
2.2: and the woman conceives, and bears a son, and she sees him that he is fair, and she hides him three months,
2.3: and she has not been able any more to hide him, and she takes for him an ark of rushes, and daubs it with bitumen and with pitch, and puts the lad in it, and puts it in the weeds by the edge of the River;
2.4: and his sister stations herself afar off, to know what is done to him.
2.5: And a daughter of Pharaoh comes down to bathe at the River, and her damsels are walking by the side of the River, and she sees the ark in the midst of the weeds, and sends her handmaid, and she takes it,
2.6: and opens, and sees him--the lad, and indeed, a child weeping! and she has pity on him, and says, `This is one of the Hebrews' children.'
2.7: And his sister says to the daughter of Pharaoh, `Do I go? when I have called for you a suckling woman of the Hebrews, then she does suckle the lad for you;'
2.8: and the daughter of Pharaoh says to her, `Go;' and the virgin goes, and calls the mother of the lad,
2.9: and the daughter of Pharaoh says to her, `Take this lad away, and suckle him for me, and I--I give your hire;' and the woman takes the lad, and suckles him.
2.10: And the lad grows, and she brings him in to the daughter of Pharaoh, and he is to her for a son, and she calls his name Moses, and says, `Because--from the water I have drawn him.'
2.11: And it comes to pass, in those days, that Moses is grown, and he goes out to his brethren, and looks on their burdens, and sees a man, an Egyptian, smiting a man, a Hebrew, one of his brethren,
2.12: and he turns here and there, and sees that there is no man, and smites the Egyptian, and hides him in the sand.
2.13: And he goes out on the second day, and indeed, two men, Hebrews, striving! and he says to the wrong-doer, `Why do you smite your neighbour?'
2.14: and he says, `Who set you for a head and a judge over us? to slay me are you saying it, as you have slain the Egyptian?' and Moses fears, and says, `Surely the thing has been known.'
2.15: And Pharaoh hears of this thing, and seeks to slay Moses, and Moses flees from the face of Pharaoh, and dwells in the land of Midian, and dwells by the well.
2.16: And to a priest of Midian are seven daughters, and they come and draw, and fill the troughs, to water the flock of their father,
2.17: and the shepherds come and drive them away, and Moses arises, and saves them, and waters their flock.
2.18: And they come in to Reuel their father, and he says, `Wherefore have you hastened to come in to-day?'
2.19: and they say, `A man, an Egyptian, has delivered us out of the hand of the shepherds, and also has diligently drawn for us, and waters the flock;'
2.20: and he says to his daughters, `And where is he? why is this? --you left the man! call for him, and he does eat bread.'
2.21: And Moses is willing to dwell with the man, and he gives Zipporah his daughter to Moses,
2.22: and she bears a son, and he calls his name Gershom, for he said, `A sojourner I have been in a strange land.'
2.23: And it comes to pass during these many days, that the king of Egypt dies, and the sons of Israel sigh because of the service, and cry, and their cry goes up to God, because of the service;
2.24: and God hears their groaning, and God remembers His covenant with Abraham, with Isaac, and with Jacob;
2.25: and God sees the sons of Israel, and God knows.

3.1: And Moses has been feeding the flock of Jethro his father-in-law, priest of Midian, and he leads the flock behind the wilderness, and comes in to the mount of God, to Horeb;
3.2: and there appears to him a messenger of Jehovah in a flame of fire, out of the midst of the bush, and he sees, and indeed, the bush is burning with fire, and the bush is not consumed.
3.3: And Moses says, `Let me turn aside, I pray you, and I see this great appearance; wherefore is the bush not burned?'
3.4: and Jehovah sees that he has turned aside to see, and God calls to him out of the midst of the bush, and says, `Moses, Moses;' and he says, `Here am I.'
3.5: And He says, `Come not near here: cast your shoes from off your feet, for the place on which you are standing is holy ground.'
3.6: He says also, `I am the God of your father, God of Abraham, God of Isaac, and God of Jacob;' and Moses hides his face, for he is afraid to look toward God.
3.7: And Jehovah says, `I have certainly seen the affliction of My people who are in Egypt, and their cry I have heard, because of its exactors, for I have known its pains;
3.8: and I go down to deliver it out of the hand of the Egyptians, and to cause it to go up out of the land, to a land good and broad, to a land flowing with milk and honey--to the place of the Canaanite, and the Hittite, and the Amorite, and the Perizzite, and the Hivite, and the Jebusite.
3.9: `And now, indeed, the cry of the sons of Israel has come in to Me, and I have also seen the oppression with which the Egyptians are oppressing them,
3.10: and now, come, and I send you to Pharaoh, and bring you out My people, the sons of Israel, out of Egypt.'
3.11: And Moses says to God, `Who am I, that I go to Pharaoh, and that I bring out the sons of Israel from Egypt?'
3.12: and He says, `Because I am with you, and this is to you the sign that I have sent you: in your bringing out the people from Egypt--you do serve God on this mount.'
3.13: And Moses says to God, `Indeed, I am coming to the sons of Israel, and have said to them, The God of your fathers has sent me to you, and they have said to me, What is His name? what do I say to them?'
3.14: And God says to Moses, `I AM THAT WHICH I AM;' He says also, `Thus do you say to the sons of Israel, I AM has sent me to you.'
3.15: And God says again to Moses, `Thus do you say to the sons of Israel, Jehovah, God of your fathers, God of Abraham, God of Isaac, and God of Jacob, has sent me to you; this is My name--to the age, and this My memorial, to generation--generation.
3.16: `Go, and you have gathered the elders of Israel, and have said to them: Jehovah, God of your fathers, has appears to me, God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, saying, I have certainly inspected you, and that which is done to you in Egypt;
3.17: and I say, I bring you up out of the affliction of Egypt, to the land of the Canaanite, and the Hittite, and the Amorite, and the Perizzite, and the Hivite, and the Jebusite, to a land flowing with milk and honey.
3.18: `And they have hearkened to your voice, and you have entered, you and the elders of Israel, to the king of Egypt, and you have said to him, Jehovah, God of the Hebrews, has met with us; and now, let us go, we pray you, a journey of three days into the wilderness, and we sacrifice to Jehovah our God.
3.19: `And I--I have known that the king of Egypt does not permit you to go, unless by a strong hand,
3.20: and I have put forth My hand, and have smitten Egypt with all My wonders, which I do in its midst--and afterwards he does send you away.
3.21: `And I have given the grace of this people in the eyes of the Egyptians, and it has come to pass, when you go, you go not empty;
3.22: and every woman has asked from her neighbour, and from her who is sojourning in her house, vessels of silver, and vessels of gold, and garments, and you have put them on your sons and on your daughters, and have spoiled the Egyptians.'

4.1: And Moses answers and says, `And, if they do not give credence to me, nor hearken to my voice, and say, Jehovah has not appeared to you?'
4.2: And Jehovah says to him, `What is this in your hand?' and he says, `A rod;'
4.3: and He says, `Cast it to the earth;' and he casts it to the earth, and it becomes a serpent--and Moses flees from its presence.
4.4: And Jehovah says to Moses, `Put forth your hand, and lay hold on the tail of it;' and he puts forth his hand, and lays hold on it, and it becomes a rod in his hand--
4.5: `--so that they believe that Jehovah, God of their fathers, has appeared to you, God of Abraham, God of Isaac, and God of Jacob.'
4.6: And Jehovah says to him again, `Put in, I pray you, your hand into your bosom;' and he puts in his hand into his bosom, and he brings it out, and indeed, his hand is leprous as snow;
4.7: and He says, `Put back your hand to your bosom;' and he puts back his hand to his bosom, and he brings it out from his bosom, and indeed, it has turned back as his flesh--
4.8: `--and it has come to pass, if they do not give credence to you, and hearken not to the voice of the first sign, that they have given credence to the voice of the latter sign.
4.9: `And it has come to pass, if they do not give credence even to these two signs, nor hearken to your voice, that you have taken of the waters of the River, and have poured on the dry land, and the waters which you take from the River have been, yes, they have become--blood on the dry land.'
4.10: And Moses says to Jehovah, `O, my Lord, I am not a man of words, either yesterday, or before, or since Your speaking to Your servant, for I am slow of mouth, and slow of tongue.'
4.11: And Jehovah says to him, `Who appointed a mouth for man? or who appoints the dumb, or deaf, or open, or blind? is it not I, Jehovah?
4.12: and now, go, and I--I am with your mouth, and have directed you that which you speak;'
4.13: and he says, `O, my Lord, send, I pray you, by the hand You do send.'
4.14: And the anger of Jehovah burns against Moses, and He says, `Is not Aaron the Levite your brother? I have known that he speaks well, and also, indeed, he is coming out to meet you; when he has seen you, then he has rejoiced in his heart,
4.15: and you have spoken to him, and have set the words in his mouth, and I--I am with your mouth, and with his mouth, and have directed you that which you do;
4.16: and he, he has spoken for you to the people, and it has come to pass, he--he is to you for a mouth, and you--you are to him for God;
4.17: and this rod you do take in your hand, with which you do the signs.'
4.18: And Moses goes and turns back to Jethro his father-in-law, and says to him, `Let me go, I pray you, and I turn back to my brethren who are in Egypt, and I see whether they are yet alive.' And Jethro says to Moses, `Go in peace.'
4.19: And Jehovah says to Moses in Midian, `Go, turn back to Egypt, for all the men have died who seek your life;'
4.20: and Moses takes his wife, and his sons, and causes them to ride on the ass, and turns back to the land of Egypt, and Moses takes the rod of God in his hand.
4.21: And Jehovah says to Moses, `In your going to turn back to Egypt, see--all the wonders which I have put in your hand--that you have done them before Pharaoh, and I--I strengthen his heart, and he does not send the people away;
4.22: and you have said to Pharaoh, Thus said Jehovah, My son, My first-born is Israel,
4.23: and I say to you, Send away My son, and he does serve Me; and--you do refuse to send him away--indeed, I am slaying your son, your first-born.'
4.24: And it comes to pass in the way, in a lodging place, that Jehovah meets him, and seeks to put him to death;
4.25: and Zipporah takes a flint, and cuts off the foreskin of her son, and causes it to touch his feet, and says, `Surely a bridegroom of blood are you to me;'
4.26: and He desists from him: then she said, `A bridegroom of blood,' in reference to the circumcision.
4.27: And Jehovah says to Aaron, `Go to meet Moses into the wilderness;' and he goes, and meets him in the mount of God, and kisses him,
4.28: and Moses declares to Aaron all the words of Jehovah with which He has sent him, and all the signs with which He has charged him.
4.29: And Moses goes--Aaron also--and they gather all the elders of the sons of Israel,
4.30: and Aaron speaks all the words which Jehovah has spoken to Moses, and does the signs before the eyes of the people;
4.31: and the people believe when they hear that Jehovah has looked after the sons of Israel, and that He has seen their affliction; and they bow and do obeisance.

5.1: And afterwards have Moses and Aaron entered, and they say to Pharaoh, `Thus said Jehovah, God of Israel, Send My people away, and they keep a feast to Me in the wilderness;'
5.2: and Pharaoh says, `Who is Jehovah, that I hearken to His voice, to send Israel away? I have not known Jehovah, and Israel also I do not send away.'
5.3: And they say, `The God of the Hebrews has met with us, let us go, we pray you, a journey of three days into the wilderness, and we sacrifice to Jehovah our God, lest He meet us with pestilence or with sword.'
5.4: And the king of Egypt says to them, `Why, Moses and Aaron, do you free the people from its works? go to your burdens.'
5.5: Pharaoh also says, `Indeed, numerous now is the people of the land, and you have caused them to cease from their burdens!'
5.6: And Pharaoh commands, on that day, the exactors among the people and its authorities, saying,
5.7: `You do not add to give straw to the people for the making of the bricks, as heretofore--they go and have gathered straw for themselves;
5.8: and the proper quantity of the bricks which they are making heretofore you do put on them, you do not diminish from it, for they are remiss, therefore they are crying, saying, Let us go, let us sacrifice to our God;
5.9: let the service be heavy on the men, and let them work at it, and not be dazzled by lying words.'
5.10: And the exactors of the people, and its authorities, go out, and speak to the people, saying, `Thus said Pharaoh, I do not give you straw,
5.11: you--go you, take for yourselves straw where you find it, for there is nothing of your service diminished.'
5.12: And the people is scattered over all the land of Egypt, to gather stubble for straw,
5.13: and the exactors are making haste, saying, `Complete your works, the matter of a day in its day, as when there is straw.'
5.14: And the authorities of the sons of Israel, whom the exactors of Pharaoh have placed over them, are beaten, saying, `Wherefore have you not completed your portion in making brick as heretofore, both yesterday and to-day?'
5.15: And the authorities of the sons of Israel come in and cry to Pharaoh, saying, `Why do you thus to your servants?
5.16: Straw is not given to your servants, and they are saying to us, Make bricks, and indeed, your servants are smitten--and your people has sinned.'
5.17: And he says, `Remiss--you are remiss, therefore you are saying, Let us go, let us sacrifice to Jehovah;
5.18: and now, go, serve; and straw is not given to you, and the measure of bricks you do give.'
5.19: And the authorities of the sons of Israel see them in affliction, saying, `You do not diminish from your bricks; the matter of a day in its day.'
5.20: And they meet Moses and Aaron standing to meet them, in their coming out from Pharaoh,
5.21: and say to them, `Jehovah look upon you, and judge, because you have caused our fragrance to stink in the eyes of Pharaoh, and in the eyes of his servants--to give a sword into their hand to slay us.'
5.22: And Moses turns back to Jehovah, and says, `Lord, why have You done evil to this people? why is this? --You have sent me!
5.23: and since I have come to Pharaoh, to speak in Your name, he has done evil to this people, and You have not at all delivered Your people.'

6.1: And Jehovah says to Moses, `Now do you see that which I do to Pharaoh, for with a strong hand he does send them away, yes, with a strong hand he does cast them out of his land.'
6.2: And God speaks to Moses, and says to him, `I am Jehovah,
6.3: and I appear to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob, as God Almighty; as to My name Jehovah, I have not been known to them;
6.4: and also I have established My covenant with them, to give to them the land of Canaan, the land of their sojournings, in which they have sojourned;
6.5: and also I have heard the groaning of the sons of Israel, whom the Egyptians are causing to serve, and I remember My covenant.
6.6: `Therefore say to the sons of Israel, I am Jehovah, and I have brought you out from under the burdens of the Egyptians, and have delivered you from their service, and have redeemed you by a stretched-out arm, and by great judgments,
6.7: and have taken you to Me for a people, and I have been to you for God, and you have known that I am Jehovah your God, who is bringing you out from under the burdens of the Egyptians;
6.8: and I have brought you in to the land which I have lifted up My hand to give it to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob, and have given it to you--a possession; I am Jehovah.'
6.9: And Moses speaks so to the sons of Israel, and they hearkened not to Moses, for anguish of spirit, and for harsh service.
6.10: And Jehovah speaks to Moses, saying,
6.11: `Go in, speak to Pharaoh king of Egypt, and he does send the sons of Israel out of his land;
6.12: and Moses speaks before Jehovah, saying, `Indeed, the sons of Israel have not hearkened to me, and how does Pharaoh hear me, and I of uncircumcised lips?'
6.13: And Jehovah speaks to Moses, and to Aaron, and charges them for the sons of Israel, and for Pharaoh king of Egypt, to bring out the sons of Israel from the land of Egypt.
6.14: These are heads of the house of their fathers: Sons of Reuben first-born of Israel are Hanoch, and Phallu, Hezron, and Carmi: these are families of Reuben.
6.15: And sons of Simeon are Jemuel, and Jamin, and Ohad, and Jachin, and Zohar, and Shaul, son of the Canaanitess: these are families of Simeon.
6.16: And these are the names of the sons of Levi, as to their births: Gershon, and Kohath, and Merari: and the years of the life of Levi are a hundred and thirty and seven years.
6.17: The sons of Gershon are Libni, and Shimi, as to their families.
6.18: And the sons of Kohath are Amram, and Izhar, and Hebron, and Uzziel: and the years of the life of Kohath are a hundred and thirty and three years.
6.19: And the sons of Merari are Mahli and Mushi: these are families of Levi, as to their births.
6.20: And Amram takes Jochebed his aunt to himself for a wife, and she bears to him Aaron and Moses: and the years of the life of Amram are a hundred and thirty and seven years.
6.21: And sons of Izhar are Korah, and Nepheg, and Zichri.
6.22: And sons of Uzziel are Mishael, and Elzaphan, and Sithri.
6.23: And Aaron takes Elisheba daughter of Amminadab, sister of Naashon, to himself for a wife, and she bears to him Nadab, and Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
6.24: And sons of Korah are Assir, and Elkanah, and Abiasaph: these are families of the Korhite.
6.25: And Eleazar, Aaron's son, has taken to him one of the daughters of Putiel for a wife to himself, and she bears to him Phinehas: these are heads of the fathers of the Levites, as to their families.
6.26: This is Aaron--and Moses--to whom Jehovah said, `Bring you out the sons of Israel from the land of Egypt, by their hosts;'
6.27: these are they who are speaking to Pharaoh king of Egypt, to bring out the sons of Israel from Egypt, this is Moses--and Aaron.
6.28: And it comes to pass in the day of Jehovah's speaking to Moses in the land of Egypt,
6.29: that Jehovah speaks to Moses, saying, `I am Jehovah, speak to Pharaoh king of Egypt all that I am speaking to you.'
6.30: And Moses says before Jehovah, `Indeed, I am of uncircumcised lips, and how does Pharaoh hearken to me?'

7.1: And Jehovah says to Moses, `See, I have given you a god to Pharaoh, and Aaron your brother is your prophet;
7.2: you--you do speak all that I command you, and Aaron your brother does speak to Pharaoh, and he has sent the sons of Israel out of his land.
7.3: `And I harden the heart of Pharaoh, and have multiplied My signs and My wonders in the land of Egypt,
7.4: and Pharaoh does not hearken, and I have put My hand on Egypt, and have brought out My hosts, My people, the sons of Israel, from the land of Egypt by great judgments;
7.5: and the Egyptians have known that I am Jehovah, in My stretching out My hand against Egypt; and I have brought out the sons of Israel from their midst.'
7.6: And Moses does--Aaron also--as Jehovah commanded them; so have they done;
7.7: and Moses is a son of eighty years, and Aaron is a son of eighty and three years, in their speaking to Pharaoh.
7.8: And Jehovah speaks to Moses and to Aaron, saying,
7.9: `When Pharaoh speaks to you, saying, Give for yourselves a wonder; then you have said to Aaron, Take your rod, and cast before Pharaoh--it becomes a monster.'
7.10: And Moses goes in--Aaron also--to Pharaoh, and they do so as Jehovah has commanded; and Aaron casts his rod before Pharaoh, and before his servants, and it becomes a monster.
7.11: And Pharaoh also calls for wise men, and for sorcerers; and the scribes of Egypt, they also, with their flashings, do so,
7.12: and they cast down each his rod, and they become monsters, and the rod of Aaron swallows their rods;
7.13: and the heart of Pharaoh is strong, and he has not hearkened to them, as Jehovah has spoken.
7.14: And Jehovah says to Moses, `The heart of Pharaoh has been hard, he has refused to send the people away;
7.15: go to Pharaoh in the morning, indeed, he is going out to the water, and you have stood to meet him by the edge of the River, and the rod which was turned to a serpent you do take in your hand,
7.16: and you have said to him: Jehovah, God of the Hebrews, has sent me to you, saying, Send My people away, and they serve Me in the wilderness; and indeed, you have not hearkened hitherto.
7.17: `Thus said Jehovah: By this you know that I am Jehovah; indeed, I am smiting with the rod which is in my hand, on the waters which are in the River, and they have been turned to blood,
7.18: and the fish that are in the River die, and the River has stank, and the Egyptians have been wearied of drinking waters from the River.'
7.19: And Jehovah says to Moses, `Say to Aaron, Take your rod, and stretch out your hand against the waters of Egypt, against their streams, against their rivers, and against their ponds, and against all their collections of waters; and they are blood--and there has been blood in all the land of Egypt, both in vessels of wood, and in those of stone.'
7.20: And Moses and Aaron do so, as Jehovah has commanded, and he lifts up his hand with the rod, and smites the waters which are in the River, before the eyes of Pharaoh, and before the eyes of his servants, and all the waters which are in the River are turned to blood,
7.21: and the fish which is in the River has died, and the River stinks, and the Egyptians have not been able to drink water from the River; and the blood is in all the land of Egypt.
7.22: And the scribes of Egypt do so with their flashings, and the heart of Pharaoh is strong, and he has not hearkened to them, as Jehovah has spoken,
7.23: and Pharaoh turns and goes in to his house, and has not set his heart even to this;
7.24: and all the Egyptians seek water round about the river to drink, for they have not been able to drink of the waters of the River.
7.25: And seven days are completed after Jehovah's smiting the River,

8.1: And Jehovah says to Moses, `Go in to Pharaoh: and you have said to him, Thus said Jehovah, Send My people away, and they serve Me;
8.2: and if you are refusing to send away, indeed, I am smiting all your border with frogs;
8.3: and the River has teemed with frogs, and they have gone up and gone into your house, and into the inner-chamber of your bed, and on your couch, and into the house of your servants, and among your people, and into your ovens, and into your kneading-troughs;
8.4: yes, on you, and on your people, and on all your servants do the frogs go up.'
8.5: And Jehovah says to Moses, `Say to Aaron, Stretch out your hand, with your rod, against the streams, against the rivers, and against the ponds, and cause the frogs to come up against the land of Egypt.'
8.6: And Aaron stretches out his hand against the waters of Egypt, and the frog comes up, and covers the land of Egypt;
8.7: and the scribes do so with their flashings, and cause the frogs to come up against the land of Egypt.
8.8: And Pharaoh calls for Moses and for Aaron, and says, `Make supplication to Jehovah, that he turn aside the frogs from me, and from my people, and I send the people away, and they sacrifice to Jehovah.'
8.9: And Moses says to Pharaoh, `Beautify yourself over me; when do I make supplication for you, and for your servants, and for your people, to cut off the frogs from you and from your houses--only in the River they do remain?'
8.10: and he says, `To-morrow.' And he says, According to your word it is, so that you know that there is none like Jehovah our God,
8.11: and the frogs have turned aside from you, and from your houses, and from your servants, and from your people; only in the River they do remain.'
8.12: And Moses--Aaron also--goes out from Pharaoh, and Moses cries to Jehovah, concerning the matter of the frogs which He has set on Pharaoh;
8.13: and Jehovah does according to the word of Moses, and the frogs die out of the houses, out of the courts, and out of the fields,
8.14: and they heap them up together, and the land stinks.
8.15: And Pharaoh sees that there has been a respite, and he has hardened his heart, and has not hearkened to them, as Jehovah has spoken.
8.16: And Jehovah says to Moses, `Say to Aaron, Stretch out your rod, and smite the dust of the land, and it has become gnats in all the land of Egypt.'
8.17: And they do so, and Aaron stretches out his hand with his rod, and smites the dust of the land, and the gnats are on man and on beast; all the dust of the land has been gnats in all the land of Egypt.
8.18: And the scribes do so with their flashings, to bring out the gnats, and they have not been able, and the gnats are on man and on beast;
8.19: and the scribes say to Pharaoh, `It is the finger of God;' and the heart of Pharaoh is strong, and he has not hearkened to them, as Jehovah has spoken.
8.20: And Jehovah says to Moses, `Rise early in the morning, and station yourself before Pharaoh, indeed, he is going out to the waters, and you have said to him, Thus said Jehovah, Send My people away, and they serve Me;
8.21: for, if you are not sending My people away, indeed, I am sending against you, and against your servants, and against your people, and against your houses, the beetle, and the houses of the Egyptians have been full of the beetle, and also the ground on which they are.
8.22: `And I have separated in that day the land of Goshen, in which My people are staying, that the beetle is not there, so that you know that I am Jehovah in the midst of the land,
8.23: and I have put a division between My people and your people: to-morrow is this sign.'
8.24: And Jehovah does so, and the grievous beetle enters the house of Pharaoh, and the house of his servants, and in all the land of Egypt the land is corrupted from the presence of the beetle.
8.25: And Pharaoh calls to Moses and to Aaron, and says, `Go, sacrifice to your God in the land;'
8.26: and Moses says, `Not right to do so, for the abomination of the Egyptians we do sacrifice to Jehovah our God; indeed, we sacrifice the abomination of the Egyptians before their eyes--and they do not stone us!
8.27: A journey of three days we go into the wilderness, and have sacrificed to Jehovah our God, as He says to us.'
8.28: And Pharaoh says, `I send you away, and you have sacrificed to Jehovah your God in the wilderness, only go not very far off; make you supplication for me;'
8.29: and Moses says, `Indeed, I am going out from you, and have made supplication to Jehovah, and the beetle has turned aside from Pharaoh, from his servants, and from his people--to-morrow, only let not Pharaoh add to deceive--in not sending the people away to sacrifice to Jehovah.'
8.30: And Moses goes out from Pharaoh, and makes supplication to Jehovah,
8.31: and Jehovah does according to the word of Moses, and turns aside the beetle from Pharaoh, from his servants, and from his people--there has not been left one;
8.32: and Pharaoh hardens his heart also at this time, and has not sent the people away.

9.1: And Jehovah says to Moses, `Go in to Pharaoh, and you have spoken to him, Thus said Jehovah, God of the Hebrews, Send My people away, and they serve me,
9.2: for, if you are refusing to send away, and are still keeping hold upon them,
9.3: indeed, the hand of Jehovah is on your cattle which are in the field, on horses, on asses, on camels, on herd, and on flock--a pestilence very grievous.
9.4: `And Jehovah has separated between the cattle of Israel and the cattle of Egypt, and there does not die a thing of all the sons of Israel's;
9.5: and Jehovah sets an appointed time, saying, To-morrow does Jehovah do this thing in the land.'
9.6: And Jehovah does this thing on the morrow, and all the cattle of Egypt die, and of the cattle of the sons of Israel not one has died;
9.7: and Pharaoh sends, and indeed, not even one of the cattle of Israel has died, and the heart of Pharaoh is hard, and he has not sent the people away.
9.8: And Jehovah says to Moses and to Aaron, `Take to you the fulness of your hands of soot of a furnace, and Moses has sprinkled it toward the heavens, before the eyes of Pharaoh,
9.9: and it has become small dust over all the land of Egypt, and it has become on man and on cattle a boil breaking forth with blains, in all the land of Egypt.'
9.10: And they take the soot of the furnace, and stand before Pharaoh, and Moses sprinkles it toward the heavens, and it is a boil with blains, breaking forth, on man and on beast;
9.11: and the scribes have not been able to stand before Moses, because of the boil, for the boil has been on the scribes, and on all the Egyptians.
9.12: And Jehovah strengthens the heart of Pharaoh, and he has not hearkened to them, as Jehovah has spoken to Moses.
9.13: And Jehovah says to Moses, `Rise early in the morning, and station yourself before Pharaoh, and you have said to him, Thus said Jehovah, God of the Hebrews, Send My people away, and they serve Me,
9.14: for, at this time I am sending all My plagues to your heart, and on your servants, and on your people, so that you know that there is none like Me in all the earth,
9.15: for now I have put forth My hand, and I smite you, and your people, with pestilence, and you are hidden from the earth.
9.16: `And yet for this I have caused you to stand, so as to show you My power, and for the sake of declaring My Name in all the earth;
9.17: still you are exalting yourself against My people--so as not to send them away;
9.18: indeed, I am raining about this time to-morrow hail very grievous, such as has not been in Egypt, even from the day of its being founded, even until now.
9.19: `And, now, send, strengthen your cattle and all that you have in the field; every man and beast which is found in the field, and is not gathered into the house--come down on them has the hail, and they have died.'
9.20: He who is fearing the word of Jehovah among the servants of Pharaoh has caused his servants and his cattle to flee to the houses;
9.21: and he who has not set his heart to the word of Jehovah leaves his servants and his cattle in the field.
9.22: And Jehovah says to Moses, `Stretch forth your hand toward the heavens, and there is hail in all the land of Egypt, on man, and on beast, and on every herb of the field in the land of Egypt.'
9.23: And Moses stretches out his rod toward the heavens, and Jehovah has given voices and hail, and fire goes toward the earth, and Jehovah rains hail on the land of Egypt,
9.24: and there is hail, and fire catching itself in the midst of the hail, very grievous, such as has not been in all the land of Egypt since it has become a nation.
9.25: And the hail smites in all the land of Egypt all that is in the field, from man even to beast, and every herb of the field has the hail smitten, and every tree of the field it has broken;
9.26: only in the land of Goshen, where the sons of Israel are, there has been no hail.
9.27: And Pharaoh sends, and calls for Moses and for Aaron, and says to them, `I have sinned this time, Jehovah is the Righteous, and I and my people are the Wicked,
9.28: make you supplication to Jehovah, and plead that there be no voices of God and hail, and I send you away, and you add not to remain.'
9.29: And Moses says to him, `At my going out of the city, I spread my palms to Jehovah--the voices cease, and the hail is not any more, so that you know that the earth is Jehovah's;
9.30: but you and your servants--I have known that you are not yet afraid of the face of Jehovah God.'
9.31: And the flax and the barley have been smitten, for the barley is budding, and the flax forming flowers,
9.32: and the wheat and the rye have not been smitten, for they are late.
9.33: And Moses goes out from Pharaoh, from the city, and spreads his hands to Jehovah, and the voices and the hail cease, and rain has not been poured out to the earth;
9.34: and Pharaoh sees that the rain has ceased, and the hail and the voices, and he continues to sin, and hardens his heart, he and his servants;
9.35: and the heart of Pharaoh is strong, and he has not sent the sons of Israel away, as Jehovah has spoken by the hand of Moses.

10.1: And Jehovah says to Moses, `Go in to Pharaoh, for I have declared hard his heart, and the heart of his servants, so that I set these My signs in their midst,
10.2: and so that you recount in the ears of your son, and of your son's son, that which I have done in Egypt, and My signs which I have set among them, and you have known that I am Jehovah.'
10.3: And Moses comes in--Aaron also--to Pharaoh, and they say to him, `Thus said Jehovah, God of the Hebrews, Until when have you refused to be humbled at My presence? send My people away, and they serve Me,
10.4: for if you are refusing to send My people away, indeed, I am bringing in to-morrow the locust into your border,
10.5: and it has covered the eye of the land, and none is able to see the land, and it has eaten the remnant of that which is escaped, which is left to you from the hail, and it has eaten every tree which is springing for you out of the field;
10.6: and they have filled your houses, and the houses of all your servants, and the houses of all the Egyptians, which neither your fathers nor your father's fathers have seen, since the day of their being on the ground to this day,' --and he turns and goes out from Pharaoh.
10.7: And the servants of Pharaoh say to him, `Until when does this one become a snare to us? send the men away, and they serve Jehovah their God; do you not know yet that Egypt has perished?'
10.8: And Moses is brought back--Aaron also--to Pharaoh, and he says to them, `Go, serve Jehovah your God; --who and who are those going?'
10.9: And Moses says, `With our young ones, and with our aged ones, we go, with our sons, and with our daughters, with our flock, and our herd, we go, for we have a festival to Jehovah.'
10.10: And he says to them, `Be it so, Jehovah be with you when I send you and your infants away; see--for evil is before your faces;
10.11: not so! go now, you who are men, and serve Jehovah, for that you are seeking;' and one casts them out from the presence of Pharaoh.
10.12: And Jehovah says to Moses, `Stretch out your hand against the land of Egypt for the locust, and it goes up against the land of Egypt, and does eat every herb of the land--all that the hail has left.'
10.13: And Moses stretches out his rod against the land of Egypt, and Jehovah has led an east wind over the land all that day, and all the night; the morning has been, and the east wind has lifted up the locust.
10.14: And the locust goes up against all the land of Egypt, and rests in all the border of Egypt--very grievous: before it there has not been such a locust as it, and after it there is none such;
10.15: and it covers the eye of all the land, and the land is darkened; and it eats every herb of the land, and all the fruit of the trees which the hail has left, and there has not been left any green thing in the trees, or in the herb of the field, in all the land of Egypt.'
10.16: And Pharaoh hastes to call for Moses and for Aaron, and says, `I have sinned against Jehovah your God, and against you,
10.17: and now, bear with, I pray you, my sin, only this time, and make you supplication to Jehovah your God, that He turn aside from off me only this death.'
10.18: And he goes out from Pharaoh, and makes supplication to Jehovah,
10.19: and Jehovah turns a very strong sea wind, and it lifts up the locust, and blows it into the Red Sea--there has not been left one locust in all the border of Egypt;
10.20: and Jehovah strengthens the heart of Pharaoh, and he has not sent the sons of Israel away.
10.21: And Jehovah says to Moses, `Stretch out your hand toward the heavens, and there is darkness over the land of Egypt, and the darkness is felt.'
10.22: And Moses stretches out his hand toward the heavens, and there is darkness--thick darkness in all the land of Egypt three days;
10.23: they have not seen one another, and none has risen from his place three days; and to all the sons of Israel there has been light in their dwellings.'
10.24: And Pharaoh calls to Moses and says, `Go you, serve Jehovah, only your flock and your herd are stayed, your infants also go with you;'
10.25: and Moses says, `You also do give in our hand sacrifices and burnt-offerings, and we have prepared for Jehovah our God;
10.26: and also our cattle does go with us, there is not left a hoof, for from it we do take to serve Jehovah our God; and we--we know not how we do serve Jehovah till our going there.'
10.27: And Jehovah strengthens the heart of Pharaoh, and he has not been willing to send them away;
10.28: and Pharaoh says to him, `Go from me, take heed to yourself, add not to see my face, for in the day you see my face you die;'
10.29: and Moses says, `Rightly have you spoken, I add not any more to see your face.'

11.1: And Jehovah says to Moses, `One plague more I do bring in on Pharaoh, and on Egypt, afterwards he does send you away from this; when he is sending you away, he surely casts you out altogether from this place;
11.2: speak, I pray you, in the ears of the people, and they ask--each man from his neighbour, and each woman from her neighbour, vessels of silver, and vessels of gold.'
11.3: And Jehovah gives the grace of the people in the eyes of the Egyptians; also the man Moses is very great in the land of Egypt, in the eyes of the servants of Pharaoh, and in the eyes of the people.
11.4: And Moses says, `Thus said Jehovah, About midnight I am going out into the midst of Egypt,
11.5: and every first-born in the land of Egypt has died, from the first-born of Pharaoh who is sitting on his throne, to the first-born of the maid-servant who is behind the millstones, and all the first-born of beasts;
11.6: and there has been a great cry in all the land of Egypt, such as there has not been, and such as there is not again.
11.7: `And against all the sons of Israel a dog sharpens not its tongue, from man even to beast, so that you know that Jehovah does make a separation between the Egyptians and Israel;
11.8: and all these your servants have come down to me, and bowed themselves to me, saying, Go out, you and all the people who are at your feet; and afterwards I do go out;' --and he goes out from Pharaoh in the heat of anger.
11.9: And Jehovah says to Moses, `Pharaoh does not hearken to you, so as to multiply My wonders in the land of Egypt;'
11.10: and Moses and Aaron have done all these wonders before Pharaoh, and Jehovah strengthens Pharaoh's heart, and he has not sent the sons of Israel out of his land.

12.1: And Jehovah speaks to Moses and to Aaron, in the land of Egypt, saying,
12.2: `This month is to you the chief of months--it is the first to you of the months of the year;
12.3: speak you to all the company of Israel, saying, In the tenth of this month--they take to them each man a lamb for the house of the fathers, a lamb for a house.
12.4: `(And if the household be too few for a lamb, then has he taken, he and his neighbour who is near to his house, for the number of persons, each according to his eating you do count for the lamb,)
12.5: a lamb, a perfect one, a male, a son of a year, let be to you; from the sheep or from the goats you do take it.
12.6: `And it has become a charge to you, until the fourteenth day of this month, and the whole assembly of the company of Israel have slaughtered it between the evenings;
12.7: and they have taken of the blood, and have put on the two side-posts, and on the lintel over the houses in which they eat it.
12.8: `And they have eaten the flesh in this night, roast with fire; with unleavened things and bitters they do eat it;
12.9: you do not eat of it raw, or boiled at all in water, but roast with fire, its head with its legs, and with its inwards;
12.10: and you do not leave of it till morning, and that which is remaining of it till morning with fire you do burn.
12.11: `And thus you do eat it: your loins girded, your sandals on your feet, and your staff in your hand, and you have eaten it in haste; it is Jehovah's passover,
12.12: and I have passed over through the land of Egypt during this night, and have smitten every first-born in the land of Egypt, from man even to beast, and on all the gods of Egypt I do judgments; I am Jehovah.
12.13: `And the blood has become a sign for you on the houses where you are, and I have seen the blood, and have passed over you, and a plague is not on you for destruction in My smiting in the land of Egypt.
12.14: `And this day has become to you a memorial, and you have kept it a feast to Jehovah to your generations; --a statute age-during; you keep it a feast.
12.15: Seven days you eat unleavened things; only--in the first day you cause leaven to cease out of your houses; for any one eating anything fermented from the first day till the seventh day, even that person has been cut off from Israel.
12.16: `And in the first day is a holy convocation, and in the seventh day you have a holy convocation; any work is not done in them, only that which is eaten by any person--it alone is done by you,
12.17: and you have observed the unleavened things, for in this self-same day I have brought out your hosts from the land of Egypt, and you have observed this day to your generations--a statute age-during.
12.18: `In the first month, in the fourteenth day of the month, in the evening, you do eat unleavened things until the one and twentieth day of the month, at evening;
12.19: seven days leaven is not found in your houses, for any one eating anything fermented--that person has been cut off from the company of Israel, among the sojourners or among the natives of the land;
12.20: anything fermented you do not eat, in all your dwellings you do eat unleavened things.'
12.21: And Moses calls for all the elders of Israel, and says to them, `Draw out and take for yourselves from the flock, for your families, and slaughter the passover-sacrifice;
12.22: and you have taken a bunch of hyssop, and have dipped it in the blood which is in the basin, and have struck it on the lintel, and on the two side-posts, from the blood which is in the basin, and you, you go not out each from the opening of his house till morning.
12.23: `And Jehovah has passed on to smite the Egyptians, and has seen the blood on the lintel, and on the two side-posts, and Jehovah has passed over the opening, and does not permit the destruction to come into your houses to smite.
12.24: `And you have observed this thing, for a statute to you, and to your sons--to the age;
12.25: and it has been, when you come in to the land which Jehovah gives to you, as He has spoken, that you have kept this service;
12.26: and it has come to pass when your sons say to you, What is this service you have?
12.27: that you have said, A sacrifice of passover it is to Jehovah, who passed over the houses of the sons of Israel in Egypt, in His smiting the Egyptians, and our houses He delivered.'
12.28: And the people bow and do obeisance, and the sons of Israel go and do as Jehovah commanded Moses and Aaron; so have they done.
12.29: And it comes to pass, at midnight, that Jehovah has smitten every first-born in the land of Egypt, from the first-born of Pharaoh who is sitting on his throne, to the first-born of the captive who is in the prison-house, and every first-born of beasts.
12.30: And Pharaoh rises by night, he and all his servants, and all the Egyptians, and there is a great cry in Egypt, for there is not a house where there is not one dead,
12.31: and he calls for Moses and for Aaron by night, and says, `Rise, go out from the midst of my people, both you and the sons of Israel, and go, serve Jehovah according to your word;
12.32: both your flock and your herd take you, as you have spoken, and go; then you have blessed also me.'
12.33: And the Egyptians are urgent on the people, hasting to send them away out of the land, for they said, `We are all dead;'
12.34: and the people takes up its dough before it is fermented, their kneading-troughs are bound up in their garments on their shoulder.
12.35: And the sons of Israel have done according to the word of Moses, and they ask from the Egyptians vessels of silver and vessels of gold, and garments;
12.36: and Jehovah has given the grace of the people in the eyes of the Egyptians, and they cause them to ask, and they spoil the Egyptians.
12.37: And the sons of Israel journey from Rameses to Succoth, about six hundred thousand men on foot, apart from infants;
12.38: and a great rabble also has gone up with them, and flock and herd--very much cattle.
12.39: And they bake with the dough which they have brought out from Egypt unleavened cakes, for it has not fermented; for they have been cast out of Egypt, and have not been able to delay, and also provision they have not made for themselves.
12.40: And the dwelling of the sons of Israel which they have dwelt in Egypt is four hundred and thirty years;
12.41: and it comes to pass, at the end of four hundred and thirty years--yes, it comes to pass in this self-same day--all the hosts of Jehovah have gone out from the land of Egypt.
12.42: A night of watchings it is to Jehovah, to bring them out from the land of Egypt; it is this night to Jehovah of watchings to all the sons of Israel to their generations.
12.43: And Jehovah says to Moses and Aaron, `This is a statute of the passover; Any son of a stranger does not eat of it;
12.44: and any man's servant, the purchase of money, when you have circumcised him--then he does eat of it;
12.45: a settler or hired servant does not eat of it;
12.46: in one house it is eaten, you do not carry out of the house any of the flesh without, and a bone you do not break of it;
12.47: all the company of Israel do keep it.
12.48: `And when a sojourner sojourns with you, and has made a passover to Jehovah, every male of his is to be circumcised, and then he does come near to keep it, and he has been as a native of the land, but any uncircumcised one does not eat of it;
12.49: one law is to a native, and to a sojourner who is sojourning in your midst.'
12.50: And all the sons of Israel do as Jehovah commanded Moses and Aaron; so have they done.
12.51: And it comes to pass in this self-same day, Jehovah has brought out the sons of Israel from the land of Egypt, by their hosts.

13.1: And Jehovah speaks to Moses, saying,
13.2: `Sanctify to Me every first-born, opening any womb among the sons of Israel, among man and among beast; it is Mine.'
13.3: And Moses says to the people, `Remember this day in which you have gone out from Egypt, from the house of servants, for by strength of hand has Jehovah brought you out from this, and any thing fermented is not eaten;
13.4: To-day you are going out, in the month of Abib.
13.5: `And it has been, when Jehovah brings you in to the land of the Canaanite, and of the Hittite, and of the Amorite, and of the Hivite, and of the Jebusite, which He has sworn to your fathers to give to you, a land flowing with milk and honey, that you have done this service in this month.
13.6: `Seven days you do eat unleavened things, and in the seventh day is a feast to Jehovah;
13.7: unleavened things are eaten the seven days, and any thing fermented is not seen with you; yes, leaven is not seen with you in all your border.
13.8: `And you have declared to your son in that day, saying, ` It is because of what Jehovah did to me, in my going out from Egypt,
13.9: and it has been to you for a sign on your hand, and for a memorial between your eyes, so that the law of Jehovah is in your mouth, for by a strong hand has Jehovah brought you out from Egypt;
13.10: and you have kept this statute at its appointed season from days to days.
13.11: `And it has been, when Jehovah brings you in to the land of the Canaanite, as He has sworn to you and to your fathers, and has given it to you,
13.12: that you have caused every one opening a womb to pass over to Jehovah, and every firstling--the increase of beasts which you have: the males are Jehovah's.
13.13: `And every firstling of an ass you do ransom with a lamb, and if you do not ransom it, then you have beheaded it: and every first-born of man among your sons you do ransom.
13.14: `And it has been, when your son asks you hereafter, saying, What is this? that you have said to him, By strength of hand has Jehovah brought us out from Egypt, from a house of servants;
13.15: yes, it comes to pass, when Pharaoh has been pained to send us away, that Jehovah does slay every first-born in the land of Egypt, from the first-born of man even to the first-born of beast; therefore I am sacrificing to Jehovah all opening a womb who are males, and every first-born of my sons I ransom;
13.16: and it has been for a token on your hand, and for frontlets between your eyes, for by strength of hand has Jehovah brought us out of Egypt.'
13.17: And it comes to pass in Pharaoh's sending the people away, that God has not led them the way of the land of the Philistines, for it is near; for God said, `Lest the people repent in their seeing war, and have turned back toward Egypt;'
13.18: and God turns round the people the way of the wilderness of the Red Sea, and by fifties have the sons of Israel gone up from the land of Egypt.
13.19: And Moses takes the bones of Joseph with him, for he certainly caused the sons of Israel to swear, saying, `God does certainly inspect you, and you have brought up my bones from this with you.'
13.20: And they journey from Succoth, and encamp in Etham at the extremity of the wilderness,
13.21: and Jehovah is going before them by day in a pillar of a cloud, to lead them in the way, and by night in a pillar of fire, to give light to them, to go by day and by night;
13.22: He removes not the pillar of the cloud by day, and the pillar of the fire by night, from before the people.

14.1: And Jehovah speaks to Moses, saying,
14.2: `Speak to the sons of Israel, and they turn back and encamp before Pi-Hahiroth, between Migdol and the sea, before Baal-Zephon; over-against it you do encamp by the sea,
14.3: and Pharaoh has said of the sons of Israel, They are entangled in the land, the wilderness has shut upon them;
14.4: and I have strengthened the heart of Pharaoh, and he has pursued after them, and I am honoured on Pharaoh, and on all his force, and the Egyptians have known that I am Jehovah;' and they do so.
14.5: And it is declared to the king of Egypt that the people has fled, and the heart of Pharaoh and of his servants is turned against the people, and they say, `What is this we have done? that we have sent Israel away from our service.'
14.6: And he harnesses his chariot, and his people he has taken with him,
14.7: and he takes six hundred chosen chariots, even all the chariots of Egypt, and captains over them all;
14.8: and Jehovah strengthens the heart of Pharaoh king of Egypt, and he pursues after the sons of Israel, and the sons of Israel are going out with a high hand,
14.9: and the Egyptians pursue after them, and all the chariot horses of Pharaoh, and his horsemen, and his force, overtake them, encamping by the sea, by Pi-Hahiroth, before Baal-Zephon.
14.10: And Pharaoh has drawn near, and the sons of Israel lift up their eyes, and indeed, the Egyptians are journeying after them, and they fear exceedingly, and the sons of Israel cry to Jehovah.
14.11: And they say to Moses, `Because there are no graves in Egypt, have you taken us away to die in a wilderness? what is this you have done to us--to bring us out from Egypt?
14.12: Is not this the word which we spoke to you in Egypt, saying, Cease from us, and we serve the Egyptians; for better for us to serve the Egyptians than to die in a wilderness?'
14.13: And Moses says to the people, `Fear not, station yourselves, and see the salvation of Jehovah, which He does for you to-day; for, as you have seen the Egyptians to-day, you add no more to see them--to the age;
14.14: Jehovah does fight for you, and you keep silent.'
14.15: And Jehovah says to Moses, `What? you cry to Me--speak to the sons of Israel, and they journey;
14.16: and you, lift up your rod, and stretch out your hand toward the sea, and cleave it, and the sons of Israel go into the midst of the sea on dry land.
14.17: `And I--indeed, I am strengthening the heart of the Egyptians, and they go in after them, and I am honoured on Pharaoh, and on all his force, on his chariots, and on his horsemen;
14.18: and the Egyptians have known that I am Jehovah, in My being honoured on Pharaoh, on his chariots, and on his horsemen.'
14.19: And the messenger of God, who is going before the camp of Israel, journeys and goes at their rear; and the pillar of the cloud journeys from their front, and stands at their rear,
14.20: and comes in between the camp of the Egyptians and the camp of Israel, and the cloud and the darkness are, and he enlightens the night, and the one has not drawn near to the other all the night.
14.21: And Moses stretches out his hand toward the sea, and Jehovah causes the sea to go on by a strong east wind all the night, and makes the sea become dry ground, and the waters are cleaved,
14.22: and the sons of Israel go into the midst of the sea, on dry land, and the waters are to them a wall, on their right and on their left.
14.23: And the Egyptians pursue, and go in after them (all the horses of Pharaoh, his chariots, and his horsemen) to the midst of the sea,
14.24: and it comes to pass, in the morning watch, that Jehovah looks to the camp of the Egyptians through the pillar of fire and of the cloud, and troubles the camp of the Egyptians,
14.25: and turns aside the wheels of their chariots, and they lead them with difficulty, and the Egyptians say, `Let us flee from the face of Israel, for Jehovah is fighting for them against the Egyptians.'
14.26: And Jehovah says to Moses, `Stretch out your hand toward the sea, and the waters turn back on the Egyptians, on their chariots, and on their horsemen.'
14.27: And Moses stretches out his hand toward the sea, and the sea turns back, at the turning of the morning, to its perennial flow, and the Egyptians are fleeing at its coming, and Jehovah shakes off the Egyptians in the midst of the sea,
14.28: and the waters turn back, and cover the chariots and the horsemen, even all the force of Pharaoh, who are coming in after them into the sea--there has not been left of them even one.
14.29: And the sons of Israel have gone on dry land in the midst of the sea, and the waters are to them a wall, on their right and on their left;
14.30: and Jehovah saves Israel in that day out of the hand of the Egyptians, and Israel sees the Egyptians dead on the sea-shore,
14.31: and Israel sees the great hand with which Jehovah has worked against the Egyptians, and the people fear Jehovah, and remain stedfast in Jehovah, and in Moses His servant.

15.1: Then sings Moses and the sons of Israel this song to Jehovah, and they speak, saying: --`I sing to Jehovah, For triumphing He has triumphed; The horse and its rider He has thrown into the sea.
15.2: My strength and song is JAH, And He is become my salvation: This is my God, and I glorify Him; God of my father, and I exalt Him.
15.3: Jehovah is a man of battle; Jehovah is His name.
15.4: Chariots of Pharaoh and his force He has cast into the sea; And the choice of his captains Have sunk in the Red Sea!
15.5: The depths do cover them; They went down into the depths as a stone.
15.6: Your right hand, O Jehovah, Is become honourable in power; Your right hand, O Jehovah, Does crush an enemy.
15.7: And in the abundance of Your excellency You throw down Your withstanders, You send forth Your wrath--It consumes them as stubble.
15.8: And by the spirit of Your anger Have waters been heaped together; Stood as a heap have flowings; Congealed have been depths In the heart of a sea.
15.9: The enemy said, I pursue, I overtake; I apportion spoil; Filled is my soul with them; I draw out my sword; My hand destroys them: --
15.10: You have blown with Your wind The sea has covered them; They sank as lead in mighty waters.
15.11: Who is like You among the gods, O Jehovah? Who is like You--honourable in holiness--Fearful in praises--doing wonders?
15.12: You have stretched out Your right hand--Earth swallows them!
15.13: You have led forth in Your kindness The people whom You have redeemed. You have led on in Your strength To Your holy habitation.
15.14: Peoples have heard, they are troubled; Pain has seized inhabitants of Philistia.
15.15: Then have chiefs of Edom been troubled: Mighty ones of Moab--Trembling does seize them! Melted have all inhabitants of Canaan!
15.16: Fall on them does terror and dread; By the greatness of Your arm They are still as a stone, Till Your people pass over, O Jehovah; Till the people pass over Whom You have purchased.
15.17: You do bring them in, And do plant them In a mountain of Your inheritance, A fixed place for Your dwelling You have made, O Jehovah; A sanctuary, O Lord, Your hands have established;
15.18: Jehovah reigns--to the age, and for ever!'
15.19: For the horse of Pharaoh has gone in with his chariots and with his horsemen into the sea, and Jehovah turns back on them the waters of the sea, and the sons of Israel have gone on dry land in the midst of the sea.
15.20: And Miriam the inspired one, sister of Aaron, takes the timbrel in her hand, and all the women go out after her, with timbrels and with choruses;
15.21: and Miriam answers to them: --`Sing you to Jehovah, For Triumphing He has triumphed; The horse and its rider He has thrown into the sea!'
15.22: And Moses causes Israel to journey from the Red Sea, and they go out to the wilderness of Shur, and they go three days in the wilderness, and have not found water,
15.23: and they come in to Marah, and have not been able to drink the waters of Marah, for they are bitter; therefore has one called its name Marah.
15.24: And the people murmur against Moses, saying, `What do we drink?'
15.25: and he cries to Jehovah, and Jehovah shows him a tree, and he casts to the waters, and the waters become sweet. There He has made for them a statute, and an ordinance, and there He has tried them,
15.26: and He says, `If you do really hearken to the voice of Jehovah your God, and do that which is right in His eyes, and have hearkened to His commands, and kept all His statutes: none of the sickness which I laid on the Egyptians do I lay on you, for I, Jehovah, am healing you.
15.27: And they come to Elim, and there are twelve fountains of water, and seventy palm trees; and they encamp there by the waters.

16.1: And they journey from Elim, and all the company of the sons of Israel come in to the wilderness of Sin, which is between Elim and Sinai, on the fifteenth day of the second month of their going out from the land of Egypt.
16.2: And all the company of the sons of Israel murmur against Moses and against Aaron in the wilderness;
16.3: and the sons of Israel say to them, `Oh that we had died by the hand of Jehovah in the land of Egypt, in our sitting by the flesh-pot, in our eating bread to satiety--for you have brought us out to this wilderness to put all this assembly to death with hunger.'
16.4: And Jehovah says to Moses, `Indeed, I am raining to you bread from the heavens--and the people have gone out and gathered the matter of a day in its day--so that I try them whether they walk in My law, or not;
16.5: and it has been on the sixth day, that they have prepared that which they bring in, and it has been double above that which they gather day by day.'
16.6: And Moses says--Aaron also--to all the sons of Israel, `Evening--and you have known that Jehovah has brought you out from the land of Egypt;
16.7: and morning--and you have seen the honour of Jehovah, in His hearing your murmurings against Jehovah, and what are we, that you murmur against us?'
16.8: And Moses says, `In Jehovah's giving to you in the evening flesh to eat, and bread in the morning to satiety--in Jehovah's hearing your murmurings, which you are murmuring against Him, and what are we? your murmurings are not against us, but against Jehovah.'
16.9: And Moses says to Aaron, `Say to all the company of the sons of Israel, Come you near before Jehovah, for He has heard your murmurings;'
16.10: and it comes to pass, when Aaron is speaking to all the company of the sons of Israel, that they turn toward the wilderness, and indeed, the honour of Jehovah is seen in the cloud.
16.11: And Jehovah speaks to Moses, saying,
16.12: `I have heard the murmurings of the sons of Israel; speak to them, saying, Between the evenings you eat flesh, and in the morning you are satisfied with bread, and you have known that I am Jehovah your God.'
16.13: And it comes to pass in the evening, that the quail comes up, and covers the camp, and in the morning there has been the lying of dew round about the camp,
16.14: and the lying of the dew goes up, and indeed, on the face of the wilderness a thin, bare thing, thin as hoar-frost on the earth.
16.15: And the sons of Israel see, and say one to another, `What is it?' for they have not known what it is; and Moses says to them, `It is the bread which Jehovah has given to you for food.
16.16: `This is the thing which Jehovah has commanded: Gather of it each according to his eating, an omer for a poll; and the number of your persons, take you each for those in his tent.'
16.17: And the sons of Israel do so, and they gather, he who is gathering much, and he who is gathering little;
16.18: and they measure with an omer, and he who is gathering much has nothing over, and he who is gathering little has no lack, each according to his eating they have gathered.
16.19: And Moses says to them, `Let no man leave of it till morning;'
16.20: and they have not hearkened to Moses, and some of them do leave of it till morning, and it brings up worms and stinks; and Moses is wroth with them.
16.21: And they gather it morning by morning, each according to his eating; when the sun has been warm, then it has melted.
16.22: And it comes to pass on the sixth day, they have gathered a second bread, two omers for one, and all the princes of the company come in, and declare to Moses.
16.23: And he says to them, `It is that which Jehovah has spoken of; a rest--a holy sabbath to Jehovah-- is to-morrow; that which you bake, bake; and that which you boil, boil; and all that is over, let rest for yourselves in charge till the morning.'
16.24: And they let it rest until the morning, as Moses has commanded, and it has not stank, and a worm has not been in it.
16.25: And Moses says, `Eat it to-day, for to-day is a sabbath to Jehovah; to-day you find it not in the field:
16.26: six days you do gather it, and in the seventh day--the sabbath--in it there is none.'
16.27: And it comes to pass on the seventh day, some of the people have gone out to gather, and have not found.
16.28: And Jehovah says to Moses, `How long have you refused to keep My commands, and My laws?
16.29: see, because Jehovah has given to you the sabbath, therefore He is giving to you on the sixth day bread of two days; abide you each in his place, no one does go out from his place on the seventh day.'
16.30: And the people rest on the seventh day,
16.31: and the house of Israel call its name Manna, and it is as coriander seed, white; and its taste is as a cake with honey.
16.32: And Moses says, `This is the thing which Jehovah has commanded: Fill the omer with it, for a charge for your generations, so that they see the bread which I have caused you to eat in the wilderness, in My bringing you out from the land of Egypt.'
16.33: And Moses says to Aaron, `Take one pot, and put there the fulness of the omer of manna, and let it rest before Jehovah, for a charge for your generations;'
16.34: as Jehovah has given commandment to Moses, so does Aaron let it rest before the Testimony, for a charge.
16.35: And the sons of Israel have eaten the manna forty years, until their coming in to the land to be inhabited; the manna they have eaten till their coming in to the extremity of the land of Canaan.
16.36: and the omer is a tenth of the ephah.

17.1: And all the company of the sons of Israel journey from the wilderness of Sin, on their journeyings, by the command of Jehovah, and encamp in Rephidim, and there is no water for the people to drink;
17.2: and the people strive with Moses, and say, `Give us water, and we drink.' And Moses says to them, `What? --you strive with me, what? --you try Jehovah?'
17.3: and the people thirst there for water, and the people murmur against Moses, and say, `Why is this? --you have brought us up out of Egypt, to put us to death, also our sons and our cattle, with thirst.'
17.4: And Moses cries to Jehovah, saying, `What do I to this people? yet a little, and they have stoned me.'
17.5: And Jehovah says to Moses, `Pass over before the people, and take with you of the elders of Israel, and your rod with which you have smitten the River take in your hand, and you have gone:
17.6: Indeed, I am standing before you there on the rock in Horeb, and you have smitten on the rock, and waters have come out from it, and the people have drunk.' And Moses does so before the eyes of the elders of Israel,
17.7: and he calls the name of the place Massah, and Meribah, because of the `strife' of the sons of Israel, and because of their `trying' Jehovah, saying, `Is Jehovah in our midst or not?'
17.8: And Amalek comes, and fights with Israel in Rephidim,
17.9: and Moses says to Joshua, `Choose for us men, and go out, fight with Amalek: to-morrow I am standing on the top of the hill, and the rod of God in my hand.'
17.10: And Joshua does as Moses has said to him, to fight with Amalek, and Moses, Aaron, and Hur, have gone up to the top of the height;
17.11: and it has come to pass, when Moses lifts up his hand, that Israel has been mighty, and when he lets his hands rest, that Amalek has been mighty.
17.12: And the hands of Moses are heavy, and they take a stone, and set it under him, and he sits on it: and Aaron and Hur have taken hold on his hands, on this side one, and on that one, and his hands are stedfast till the going in of the sun;
17.13: and Joshua weakens Amalek and his people by the mouth of the sword.
17.14: And Jehovah says to Moses, `Write this, a memorial in a Book, and set it in the ears of Joshua, that I do utterly wipe away the remembrance of Amalek from under the heavens;'
17.15: and Moses builds an altar, and calls its name Jehovah-Nissi,
17.16: and says, `Because a hand is on the throne of Jah, war is to Jehovah with Amalek from generation--generation.'

18.1: And Jethro priest of Midian, father-in-law of Moses, hears all that God has done for Moses, and for Israel his people, that Jehovah has brought out Israel from Egypt,
18.2: and Jethro, father-in-law of Moses, takes Zipporah, wife of Moses, besides her parents,
18.3: and her two sons, of whom the name of the one is Gershom, for he said, `a sojourner I have been in a strange land:'
18.4: and the name of the other is Eliezer, for, `the God of my father is for my help, and does deliver me from the sword of Pharaoh.'
18.5: And Jethro, father-in-law of Moses, comes, and his sons, and his wife, to Moses, to the wilderness where he is encamping--the mount of God;
18.6: and he says to Moses, `I, your father-in-law, Jethro, am coming to you, and your wife, and her two sons with her.'
18.7: And Moses goes out to meet his father-in-law, and bows himself, and kisses him, and they ask one at another of welfare, and come into the tent;
18.8: and Moses recounts to his father-in-law all that Jehovah has done to Pharaoh, and to the Egyptians, on account of Israel, all the travail which has found them in the way, and Jehovah does deliver them.
18.9: And Jethro rejoices for all the good which Jehovah has done to Israel, whom He has delivered from the hand of the Egyptians;
18.10: and Jethro says, `Blessed is Jehovah, who has delivered you from the hand of the Egyptians, and from the hand of Pharaoh--who has delivered this people from under the hand of the Egyptians;
18.11: now I have known that Jehovah is greater than all the gods, for in the thing they have acted proudly-- He is above them!'
18.12: And Jethro, father-in-law of Moses, takes a burnt-offering and sacrifices for God; and Aaron comes in, and all the elders of Israel, to eat bread with the father-in-law of Moses, before God.
18.13: And it comes to pass on the morrow, that Moses sits to judge the people, and the people stand before Moses, from the morning to the evening;
18.14: and the father-in-law of Moses sees all that he is doing to the people, and says, `What is this thing which you are doing to the people? wherefore are you sitting by yourself, and all the people standing by you from morning till evening?'
18.15: And Moses says to his father-in-law, `Because the people come to me to seek God;
18.16: when they have a matter, it has come to me, and I have judged between a man and his neighbour, and made known the statutes of God, and His laws.'
18.17: And the father-in-law of Moses says to him, `The thing which you are doing is not good;
18.18: you do surely wear away, both you, and this people which is with you, for the thing is too heavy for you, you are not able to do it by yourself.
18.19: `Now, hearken to my voice, I counsel you, and God is with you: be you for the people over-against God, and you have brought in the things to God;
18.20: and you have warned them concerning the statutes and the laws, and have made known to them the way in which they go, and the work which they do.
18.21: `And you--you do provide out of all the people men of ability, fearing God, men of truth, hating dishon gain, and have placed these over them, heads of thousands, heads of hundreds, heads of fifties, and heads of tens,
18.22: and they have judged the people at all times; and it has come to pass, every great matter they bring in to you, and every small matter they judge themselves; and lighten it from off yourself, and they have borne with you.
18.23: If you do this thing, and God has commanded you, then you have been able to stand, and all this people also goes in to its place in peace.'
18.24: And Moses hearkens to the voice of his father-in-law, and does all that he said,
18.25: and Moses chooses men of ability out of all Israel, and makes them chiefs over the people, heads of thousands, heads of hundreds, heads of fifties, and heads of tens,
18.26: and they have judged the people at all times; the hard matter they bring in to Moses, and every small matter they judge themselves.
18.27: And Moses sends his father-in-law away, and he goes away to his own land.

19.1: In the third month of the going out of the sons of Israel from the land of Egypt, in this day they have come into the wilderness of Sinai,
19.2: and they journey from Rephidim, and enter the wilderness of Sinai, and encamp in the wilderness; and Israel encamps there before the mount.
19.3: And Moses has gone up to God, and Jehovah calls to him out of the mount, saying, `Thus do you say to the house of Jacob, and declare to the sons of Israel,
19.4: You--you have seen that which I have done to the Egyptians, and I bear you on eagles' wings, and bring you in to Myself.
19.5: `And now, if you really hearken to My voice, then you have kept My covenant, and been to Me a peculiar treasure more than all the peoples, for all the earth is Mine;
19.6: and you--you are to Me a kingdom of priests and a holy nation: these are the words which you do speak to the sons of Israel.'
19.7: And Moses comes, and calls for the elders of the people, and sets before them all these words which Jehovah has commanded him;
19.8: and all the people answer together and say, `All that Jehovah has spoken we do;' and Moses returns the words of the people to Jehovah.
19.9: And Jehovah says to Moses, `Indeed, I am coming to you in the thickness of the cloud, so that the people hear in My speaking with you, and also believe in you to the age;' and Moses declares the words of the people to Jehovah.
19.10: And Jehovah says to Moses, `Go to the people; and you have sanctified them to-day and to-morrow, and they have washed their garments,
19.11: and have been prepared for the third day; for on the third day does Jehovah come down before the eyes of all the people, on mount Sinai.
19.12: `And you have made a border for the people round about, saying, Take heed to yourselves, going up into the mount, or coming against its extremity; whoever is coming against the mount is certainly put to death;
19.13: a hand comes not against him, for he is certainly stoned or shot through, whether beast or man it lives not; in the drawing out of the jubilee cornet they go up into the mount.'
19.14: And Moses comes down from the mount to the people, and sanctifies the people, and they wash their garments;
19.15: and he says to the people, `Be you prepared for the third day, come not nigh to a woman.'
19.16: And it comes to pass, on the third day, while it is morning, that there are voices, and lightnings, and a heavy cloud, on the mount, and the sound of a trumpet very strong; and all the people who are in the camp do tremble.
19.17: And Moses brings out the people to meet God from the camp, and they station themselves at the lower part of the mount,
19.18: and mount Sinai is wholly a smoke from the presence of Jehovah, who has come down on it in fire, and its smoke goes up as smoke of the furnace, and the whole mount trembles exceedingly;
19.19: and the sound of the trumpet is going on, and very strong; Moses speaks, and God does answer him with a voice.
19.20: And Jehovah comes down on mount Sinai, to the top of the mount, and Jehovah calls for Moses to the top of the mount, and Moses goes up.
19.21: And Jehovah says to Moses, `Go down, protest to the people, lest they break through to Jehovah to see, and many of them have fallen;
19.22: and also the priests who are coming nigh to Jehovah do sanctify themselves, lest Jehovah break forth on them.'
19.23: And Moses says to Jehovah, `The people is unable to come up to mount Sinai, for You--You have protested to us, saying, Make a border for the mount, then you have sanctified it.'
19.24: And Jehovah says to him, `Go, descend, then you have come up, you, and Aaron with you; and the priests and the people do not break through, to come up to Jehovah, lest He break forth upon them.'
19.25: And Moses goes down to the people, and says to them: --

20.1: `And God speaks all these words, saying,
20.2: I am Jehovah your God, who has brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of a house of servants.
20.3: `You have no other Gods before Me.
20.4: `You do not make to yourself a graven image, or any likeness which is in the heavens above, or which is in the earth beneath, or which is in the waters under the earth.
20.5: You do not bow yourself to them, nor serve them: for I, Jehovah your God, am a zealous God, charging iniquity of fathers on sons, on the third generation, and on the fourth, of those hating Me,
20.6: and doing kindness to thousands, of those loving Me and keeping My commands.
20.7: `You do not take up the name of Jehovah your God for a vain thing, for Jehovah acquits not him who takes up His name for a vain thing.
20.9: six days you do labour, and have done all your work,
20.10: and the seventh day is a Sabbath to Jehovah your God; you do not do any work, you, and your son, and your daughter, your man-servant, and your handmaid, and your cattle, and your sojourner who is within your gates, --
20.11: for six days has Jehovah made the heavens and the earth, the sea, and all that is in them, and rests in the seventh day; therefore has Jehovah blessed the Sabbath-day, and does sanctify it.
20.12: `Honour your father and your mother, so that your days are prolonged on the ground which Jehovah your God is giving to you.
20.16: `You do not answer against your neighbour a false testimony.
20.17: `You do not desire the house of your neighbour, you do not desire the wife of your neighbour, or his man-servant, or his handmaid, or his ox, or his ass, or anything which is your neighbour's.'
20.18: And all the people are seeing the voices, and the flames, and the sound of the trumpet, and the mount smoking; and the people see, and move, and stand afar off,
